title: Knowledge check: Actions and Business Logic

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Actions and Business Logic”?
options: Vuex is the recommended default for all new Vue 3 applications.
Keep duplicate mutable copies of the same shared fact in every component.
Use an explicit shared store for shared state, getters for derived values, and actions for deliberate updates or asynchronous work.
Pinia persists all state securely without configuration.
questions.answer_key: Use an explicit shared store for shared state, getters for derived values, and actions for deliberate updates or asynchronous work.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Actions and Business Logic directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Synchronous actions”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Keep duplicate mutable copies of the same shared fact in every component.
Use an explicit shared store for shared state, getters for derived values, and actions for deliberate updates or asynchronous work.
Pinia persists all state securely without configuration.
Vuex is the recommended default for all new Vue 3 applications.
questions.answer_key: Use an explicit shared store for shared state, getters for derived values, and actions for deliberate updates or asynchronous work.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Synchronous actions”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Actions and Business Logic” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.
